scope: Read and review all 177 native lessons, worked examples, exercises, solutions and prerequisite links for beginner clarity while preserving technical meaning. Counts are editorial review, not learner-tested mastery.

sources.title: Carnegie Mellon Eberly Center — Learning principles
sources.application: Activate prerequisite skills, connect ideas and align targeted practice with feedback.

sources.title: Carnegie Mellon Eberly Center — Teaching principles
sources.application: Expose expert steps and align objectives, instruction and assessment.

sources.title: IES What Works Clearinghouse — Organizing Instruction and Study to Improve Student Learning
sources.application: Alternate worked examples and practice, connect concrete and abstract forms and ask explanatory questions; recommendations have differing evidence levels.

sources.title: AERO — Teach explicitly, classroom examples and transcript
sources.application: Model thinking, define vocabulary, chunk explanations and reduce guidance gradually. These school examples inform presentation; they are not direct evidence for outcomes in this adult hub.

criteria: Explain the problem before specialist terms; define essential vocabulary at first use.
State what earlier skill is needed and provide a concrete readiness check or short primer.
Show a complete small example and why each step follows.
Make the first exercise attemptable with supplied inputs, instructions and a way to check it.
Keep solutions explanatory and independent tasks aligned with what was taught.
Retain correct technical distinctions, TeX notation and clear clinical/authorisation boundaries.
